Container.Name: Quake2
Container.Overview:
id Software's 2001 Quake II source release, repaired to build and run on a current 64-bit Linux and packaged so you play it in a browser. Picture and sound both arrive over one port; the mouse is captured, and a game controller works on a phone as well as a desktop.
You supply the game data. Quake II's is id Software's and not free to redistribute, so point the Game data path below at your own Quake II install, the directory holding baseq2/pak0.pak (id's free demo works too). Without it the container stops and says so.
The mission packs, The Reckoning and Ground Zero, play with their own game code, which the image carries: put xatrix/ or rogue/ beside baseq2 and set Game to xatrix or rogue.
Music is optional and separate: Quake II's soundtrack was audio tracks on the CD, so put a rip in baseq2/music as track02.ogg and friends. The GOG release's music folder is found by itself.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: noVNC and the sound, on one port. Open http://[IP]:[PORT]/play.html

Config.Name: Game data
Config.Description: Your Quake II install: the directory holding baseq2/pak0.pak. CTF, mods and a music/ folder go beside baseq2. Mounted read-only; nothing is ever written here.

Config.Name: Width
Config.Description: Starting render width, 320 to 1920. The renderer is in software, so every pixel costs; the browser scales whatever it is given to fit the window. Options - Video in the game changes the resolution while it runs and remembers the choice, so after the first run this is only the starting point.

Config.Name: Game
Config.Description: Which game to start on. Leave empty for the base game; xatrix for The Reckoning, rogue for Ground Zero, ctf for Threewave CTF, or a mod directory name. The directory has to be in the game data mount.

Config.Name: VNC password
Config.Description: Optional. There is no authentication without it, and the transport is plain HTTP either way -- do not expose this to the internet.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the container runs as. 99 is nobody on Unraid.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the container runs as. 100 is users on Unraid.

Config.Name: Restart on exit
Config.Description: 1 brings the title screen back when the game exits or crashes; 0 stops the container instead.

Config.Name: VNC port
Config.Description: Optional. Raw VNC for a native client: picture only, no sound, and the pointer is not captured.
